Norway's Norges Bank, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and ValueQuest emerged as the lead investors in Quality Power Electrical Equipments' Rs 570-crore qualified institutional placement (QIP), according to sources familiar with the development.

The QIP, which opened on November 25 and closed on November 27, saw participation from several institutional investors, including Bank of India Mutual Fund, ITI Mutual Fund and Nuvama. However, the bulk of the bids came from Norges Bank, ICICI Prudential MF and ValueQuest, sources said.

Quality Power, which has a market capitalisation of nearly Rs 11,600 crore, announced that its board had approved the allotment of 39.07 lakh equity shares at an issue price of Rs 1,458.76 apiece.

The issue price represents a 5 percent discount of Rs 76.77 per share to the floor price of Rs 1,535.53, in accordance with SEBI's Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) regulations, the company said in an exchange filing.

Pantomath Capital Advisors and Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors acted as the merchant bankers to the issue.

Quality Power is engaged in providing high-voltage electrical equipment and solutions for grid connectivity and the energy transition. Its operations span power generation, transmission, distribution and automation, positioning it to benefit from investments in power infrastructure and grid modernisation.

data.title: SEBI chief on market reforms, pre-IPO trading, F&O segment and AI safeguards: Full text of interview with CNBC-Awaaz
data.description:
SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday spoke on a range of issues shaping India's capital markets at CNBC-Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh 2026. In an interview with CNBC-Awaaz Managing Editor Anuj Singhal, Pandey discussed the need to curb IPO grey market activity, the possibility of a regulated platform for pre-IPO trading, and the future of derivatives, investor protection and AI in financial markets. Here's the full text of the interaction:

Sir, more than 750 participants are among us. They have come from every corner of the country, and they represent our stock market, in a way, the growth of the last four or five years. Have a seat, sir. I'm proud, sir. "Samajh Se Investing Simple" ("Investing Made Simple Through Understanding"), the campaign you have run, has had CNBC Awaaz as a partner with SEBI, and in all of SEBI's earlier campaigns too, CNBC Awaaz has been with you. Sir, you were very busy. Yesterday you were at an event in Delhi. You are taking a flight right after this event, but you still did not cancel our program. First of all, heartfelt thanks for that.

Sir, one thing I have noticed about you is that you never evade a question. Whenever you are asked a question, you give a direct answer. Recently, the biggest reform you have taken a step toward, one of the big reforms (you have done many reforms, and the list is very long), is the one on the grey market premium in IPOs. I think that deserves a separate round of applause. You have taken some steps on how to shut down the grey market premium completely, but how will you enforce it fully, sir?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: Enforcement needs will, and we have the will.

Absolutely, you have the will. But sir, the IPO market has seen the most growth in the last three to four years, and retail investors, who come first (everyone who has come here puts the most money into IPOs), do you think this IPO market is healthy in our country, and do you think more steps need to be taken on this?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: One suggestion that came to us, which we are considering, is to set up a separate exchange, a trading exchange, for pre-IPO shares. Work on that is under way. You will get information about it soon. We will issue a consultation paper.

Well, you have already given us our first breaking news. Can you give a timeline for when this might happen, where we can trade unlisted stocks or pre-IPO stocks?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: No, it is only pre-IPO that falls within SEBI's remit. We are not covering all unlisted companies; the unlisted universe is very large, with lakhs of companies. We can make this arrangement only for those companies that are going to bring an IPO. But what will its contours be? Because even in that, we will have to bring in some investor protection measures and increase some disclosures. We are considering it, but there is now a possibility of it because we are working on it.

Okay, and will it be across the board, sir, or will it not be for SMEs and only for bigger companies, above a particular market cap? Have you thought about this?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: All I am saying is that it will be related to IPOs. If it is not linked to an IPO, we will not get into it.

Absolutely, sir. You have taken many steps, including the move from T+2 to T+1 and toward T+0. By when do you think we will shift fully to T+1 and T+0 for all stocks?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: We are fully on T+1, and we were the first in the world to do it. We have been on T+1 since 2023, and the US actually came in 2024. So the USA was the second one. India was the first one in 2023. The US came in 2024. Europe is also going to do it. So T+1 is fully in place.

T+1 is fully in place. You have also run some pilot tests for T+0.

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: It was optional (an optional system was in place). But there are some difficulties, because we want the market to be one comprehensive market, in which domestic institutional investors are there, foreign participants are there, and retail investors are there. Things should work according to everyone's convenience, and we also have to look at international time zones. So considering all this, we felt that if we go to T+0 now, it would become more disorderly, because keeping many options open is also problematic. Either it has to be made compulsory, and making it compulsory would cause so much difficulty to many market participants that our market's liquidity could fall.

Sir, it has been over a year and a half now. As SEBI chief, you have done many reforms. You have resolved many old stuck matters, such as the NSE IPO. There were many things that needed conviction, which you provided. What do you think is your unfinished agenda now? Do you think more reforms are needed?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: I said in my address that, look, choosing "we will do this, we will do that" is not possible here. Technology is... the technology movement is relentless. So now, as AI is arriving, that is our biggest focus area at this time: AI has many use cases and also many risks. How do we move India ahead in the system, so that we can set a model for the world? So we have to use technology, but we are also considering how to defend ourselves against that technology. Our advisory committee is looking into this. And as I mentioned, we are indeed bringing AI guidelines, which will be based on the IOSCO supervisory toolkit. But we are thinking of one more step: what if we arrange for a model, a domestic model? Many of our intermediaries would be able to use it safely, because in that model we could build in the guardrails. For that, of course, compute also needs to be arranged. It will need the cooperation of many people. So if we feel this is feasible and we can do it, I think we will be able to use AI more in the market, and do so safely.

Sir, a question you are often asked, on F&O (CNBC Awaaz also took part in this initiative): 93% of traders lose money. We show that disclaimer prominently even though 90% of our audience are traders. Even then, we show that disclaimer two or three times in every show. Despite all this, do you feel the F&O fever is still not subsiding and that some more strictness is needed, or have you reached the stage where you would say, "we have done a lot from our side, now the public has to understand"?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: Anuj ji, you have specialized in F&O, so your favorite topic, you have brought it up again. Our futures and options should have depth, which is an important market. So we need to do more of long-term options and long-term futures, and short-dated options are also traded, not in our market alone but in other markets too. And how to regulate the market so that it remains a market and moves forward in a good way. Because killing a market, forcibly shutting it down, we feel, would not be appropriate, because it also takes a lot of time to build a market, and we need to think about which direction we incentivize and motivate the market in, so that all kinds of options are available for hedging. Right now, the typical futures market for hedging, I think, is still underdeveloped in India. There are very few long-term futures. There are several reasons for it, in the way we are doing things; our margins could be one, and taxes could also be reasons. But whatever it is, we should work toward keeping depth in our derivatives market and having new products keep coming.

Because we have become the world leader in options at this time.

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: Education is also very important, because, as I said about anything, the investor should know what is right for them and not be copying someone else out of imitation. To make that happen, I think we need a certain higher level of depth, and I am confident that our young generation, given how receptive they are, will certainly learn about it if we provide them good means of learning. But those means should be interesting, something they can grasp quickly and that also generates their interest. That is why I feel the "Samajh Se Investing Simple" campaign is just a first way of connecting people, but its purpose is to take them to resources, whether digital resources or websites; we have our micro website.

We want to start our own YouTube channels in all languages, with interesting content on every subject, which people can engage with interactively, and we will use AI too, so that people can quickly get accurate information about it. Then people will have to think about how they should do their financial planning. And it is not necessary that we all stay 100% in equity. How do we diversify? Pension, insurance, fixed income, equity, REITs, InvITs, bonds: information on all these things is necessary, and people need to know that they should start investing early, at the right time and in the right way. So I feel our focus on this will be very big for the next two to three years.

And sir, in this campaign, the country's number one business channel, CNBC Awaaz, is with you, and our managing director and editor-in-chief is Rahul Joshi. I can say on his behalf too that our entire Network18, which is the country's biggest network at this time, whether digital or TV, is with this initiative of yours. There was a suggestion, from Nitesh bhai, who is here from Kotak Mutual Fund. He once gave a suggestion about weekly expiry. You said long-dated options are needed, that people should move more toward long-dated options, but weekly options should also remain, short-dated ones, as you said just now. Can something be done so that a Jane Street-type episode does not happen again, such as restricting weekly options to institutions only and taking monthly options for retail? Would that be a right attempt?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: We have not considered this yet. For a long time I kept this subject somewhat on the back burner, because all of you in the markets and the channels love that it be broadcast two or three times on each weekday of every week. I think you should take "Samajh Se Investing Simple" and, even if it is boring news, make interesting news out of it and give it to us.

No sir, we absolutely... There, you know, a dichotomy arises, because as the saying goes, if the horse befriends the grass, what will it eat? But we have made our full effort from our side. We have made our full effort from our side. We have shown the disclaimer twice in every show, prominently, that there is risk involved in F&O trading, and we have talked about it. One last topic, sir, and I know that you normally don't go into specifics, but if you would like to decline, I won't press. Yesterday at an event you spoke about the recent Tata Steel and APL Apollo deal, because minority shareholders were quite shocked. Not only minority shareholders; I would say even the institutions that were invested in it were quite shocked. It is very rare that even a SEBI chief says we are looking at a particular deal. Were you really that disappointed with this deal?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: No, when we say minority interest, everyone is included. It is not only retail; institutions are also included.

For the protection of minority shareholders, there is a provision that if related party transactions are taking place, they need a majority-of-the-minority approval. It goes to the shareholders, and the promoters and interested groups sit out; that is, they do not vote. And on related party transactions, our issue is form and substance: it is not just the form in which you are presenting it, but what the intent is. So, under our amendments of 2023, it is important to look behind the transactions to determine whether or not they fall under RPT. So I feel everyone will have to act only under these rules and regulations of ours, and if any corporate governance lapse goes beyond or short of that, we take action.

Sir, then with your permission, four quick-fire questions, if you would like to take them, rapid fire if you allow, very short four questions. First question: what is the biggest danger for an investor? Greed or leverage?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: Both.

Is the IPO market in India perfectly fine, or are issues coming at quite high valuations in India? Are IPO prices right, or are IPOs being priced quite aggressively, in your view?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: IPO prices have to be decided by investors. It is not necessary to participate in every IPO if you don't find the pricing right. We have said that if you can't read the big prospectus, we made an abridged prospectus. We gave a QR code in it, and you can see it immediately. So people need to know before investing in anything. "Samajh Se Investing Simple." So I think for investing you will have to read and look, and it is not necessary for every person to invest in everything. I have also said that there should be no FOMO. When people choose, the pricing will correct itself. I think mutual funds and domestic institutional investors do their own exercise quite a lot now and look at the pricing, because when they become anchor investors, they look at those prices, and this also falls under their stewardship code. Since they are investing on behalf of investors, they should invest only at the right pricing. So I feel it is not possible for a regulator to say whether this pricing is right or not. We only get disclosures made, and our effort has been to include in the disclosures all the important information you need, even in the draft abridged prospectus, so that those things are there.

Do you think there is healthy competition among exchanges in India?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: I think, in the way we have structured exchanges, both competition and cooperation are needed, which we call co-opetition. In services they can provide efficiency, but in connectivity, under our rules, all the exchanges, all the depositories and all the clearing corporations are connected with each other, and we have connected them through regulation. That is so that we can give best pricing to investors. They can clear anywhere and trade anywhere. So in this whole system we cannot say that they will operate entirely independently.

In many places they will have to cooperate with each other. For instance, there is the collective submission platform (SAMAVESH-type single-window filing). If you incur a penalty on one exchange, the penalty falls in only one place. We are saying that you should file in only one place. You shouldn't have to file repeatedly. So none of our ease-of-doing-business measures will be possible unless the exchanges cooperate with each other, because they have to build that network.

So I feel that in the markets we are not dependent on exactly one entity in complete monopoly, that we have other options as well. And second, there are the safety mechanisms we have put in place: your disaster recovery site is nearby, then there is a far site or one in other cities. If you make disaster recovery compulsory, that creates a second safety mechanism. So we have to keep thinking that the technology, network and connectivity arrangements in the market stay in such a way that we can face any risk.

One last question: you listed many reforms that you are planning. Is there one reform you have done that is closest to your heart? You have done many reforms. Which reform of the last year and a half is closest to your heart?

Tuhin Kanta Pandey: I simply don't answer questions of this kind where I have to think so much and have to think about whom I would pick... It's the same as if you asked which of your two sons you like more. I think that kind of thing...

We used to ask our parents, but they would give the same answer: when you have children, then you will ask this question and your answer will be the same. Sir, thank you so much for giving us so much time and for joining us at CNBC Awaaz. Thank you very much. Standing ovation please.

data.title: Planning India-made AI model for securities market: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey
data.description:
SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the market regulator is exploring the possibility of developing a separate artificial intelligence (AI) model tailored to the needs of the securities market, with a focus on data confidentiality.

Speaking at the CNBC-Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh 2026 event, Pandey said, "Today, new models of artificial intelligence are being introduced, but the worry that whether our data will be confidential always persists. For this, according to the securities market, we are looking for an opportunity to bring a different AI model that caters to these needs."

"We want that such a model is developed in India and is a part of digital public infrastructure," he added.

The SEBI chairman stated that they are working on creating a training program for this and said, "We need to work on expertise. For the engineers, who look after the securities operations, we are planning to start a training program in association with Rashtriya Raksha University and NISM. Through this training program, they will be able to learn AI tools to analyse the alerts, learn how to send automated response and how cyber security can be enhanced."

The proposed training programme will focus on helping engineers use AI tools to analyse alerts, automate responses and strengthen cybersecurity in securities market operations.

data.title: SEBI chief bats for simpler investment process, says there's need to deepen F&O segment
data.description:
SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said that simplifying the investment process and removing unnecessary regulations are among the regulator's core priorities, as participation in India's securities markets continues to grow.

Speaking at CNBC-Awaaz's 'Market Mahakumbh' event, Pandey said the regulator has taken several steps to encourage investors while protecting their interests. He also highlighted initiatives aimed at making it easier for listed companies and brokers to operate.

Pandey cited efforts to introduce a single filing system for listed companies and brokers, speed up settlement processes and simplify listing regulations.

Pandey added that there was a need to deepen the futures and options (F&O) segment and argued against forcibly shutting down any market segment. Instead, he stressed the importance of investor awareness and informed participation.

On the APL Apollo-Tata Steel deal, he said protecting minority shareholders' interests was important and that all parties must operate within the regulatory framework.

'Unique investors quadrupled since FY19'

Pandey said interest in equity markets has been growing, with more than 6,700 companies listed in India. The number of unique investors in the market has quadrupled since financial year 2018-19, he said.

With participation increasing, Pandey said regulatory frameworks also needed to evolve to ensure that investing becomes simpler and investors do not face unnecessary hurdles.

Simplifying investment rules

He said several measures had been introduced to simplify the investment process, including reducing minimum investment sizes and making investments in real estate and infrastructure assets easier.

Rules governing investments through the portfolio management services (PMS) route have also been simplified, he said.

Pandey said removing unnecessary regulations remained a priority, with the aim of simplifying processes for investors and other market participants.

Focus on timely monitoring committee reports, technology

Pandey said SEBI was also emphasising on the timely submission of reports by monitoring committees and was gradually expanding the use of technology.

He also stressed the importance of data security in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), saying safeguards were needed to ensure that the use of technology did not compromise data security.

Steps to curb fraud, improve investor awareness

Pandey said SEBI had taken measures to protect investors from fraud and that maintaining transparency in the market remained a key priority.

The regulator has also undertaken several initiatives to improve investor awareness. As part of these efforts, SEBI launched its 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' campaign on October 5, aimed at educating investors about investment-related risks and frauds, he said.

data.title: Sebi chief says ‘coopetition’ is must among exchanges for interest of investors
data.description:
Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said exchanges in India need to balance competition with cooperation, arguing that both are essential for delivering efficient services and better pricing to investors.

Speaking at the CNBC-Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh 2026 event, Pandey described the model as “coopetition”, where exchanges compete in certain areas while collaborating on infrastructure and connectivity.

“I believe that the way we have structured exchanges, there is competition plus cooperation. Both are important. We call it 'Coopetition',” Pandey said.

He said exchanges, depositories and clearing corporations are interconnected through regulations to ensure investors can access markets and benefit from competitive pricing.

“When it comes to connectivity, as per the rules, all exchanges, depositories and clearing corporations are connected to each other. And we have linked them through regulation so that we can offer investors the best pricing and they can trade anywhere,” he said.

Pandey said exchanges cannot operate entirely independently in such a system and would need to cooperate across several areas, including through collective platforms.

He added that measures aimed at improving ease of doing business would also depend on cooperation among exchanges and the creation of a broader network.

Pandey added that the market infrastructure should not be overly dependent on a single exchange, stressing the importance of safeguards, resilient technological and network systems.

“We are not dependent on the complete monopoly of any one exchange. There are safety mechanisms we have put in place... we must always keep thinking about how the market's technological and network systems are structured so that we are able to tackle any risk,” he said.

data.title: Nifty rising, but are all sectors participating? How to trade sector rotation: Shubham Agarwal
data.description:
F&O Cues

Nifty is up over 10% this month and is knocking on the 26,000 door. You open your portfolio expecting a sea of green. Instead, you see a mixed picture: some sectors are flat, some are in the red, and a few are in the green.

The index is moving higher, but not every sector is participating equally. Is the rally becoming selective? Welcome to sector rotation.

Why Sector Rotation Happens

Big money never sits in one place. When a sector has run up sharply, large investors book profits and move to sectors that still have room to grow. Changes in interest rates, inflation, crude prices or global cues also shift which sectors look attractive.

This month shows it clearly. Banks led most of November's rally, with Bank Nifty hitting a record high. In the last few days, leadership has changed. Nifty IT has jumped and is now contributing the most, while sectors like FMCG and Oil & Gas have also chipped in. Nifty still closed higher, but the engine underneath had switched.

Spotting Leaders and Laggards with Price and OI

Price tells you what happened. Open Interest (OI) tells you who did it. We used this same four-way reading in our Built-Up Breadth article. Now apply it to sectors:

•       Long Build-Up (Price Up + OI Up): Fresh money is entering. This is where you want to be.

•       Short Covering (Price Up + OI Down): Sellers are exiting. The rise can be fast but often lacks staying power.

•       Long Unwinding (Price Down + OI Down): Buyers are booking profits. Tighten stops or exit.

•       Short Build-Up (Price Down + OI Up): Fresh selling. Avoid new longs here.

The rule is simple: buy sectors showing long build-up, and exit sectors slipping into long unwinding or short build-up.

Confirming Institutional Participation

One stock moving does not make a rotation. Check the futures of the heavyweight stocks in each sector. If most large IT names show long build-up together, institutions are positioning in the whole sector. If only one stock shows it, treat it as stock-specific news.

Rising OI matters because institutions trade in size. When they commit to a sector, OI expands. A sector-wide rise on falling OI usually means shorts are covering, not that new money is arriving.

Compare Every Sector with Nifty

Finally, measure each sector against the index. If Nifty rose 1% this week and a sector rose 3%, that sector is leading. If it rose only 0.2% or fell, it is lagging, even if its chart still looks fine.

Combine both filters. A sector beating Nifty with long build-up is a strong candidate. A sector trailing Nifty with long unwinding is where money is leaving.

The Takeaway

A rising Nifty does not mean every sector is rising with it. Beneath the headline, money is always moving from one sector to another.

Don't just ask whether the market is going up. Ask where the money is going.

data.title: Strong economic growth expected in Q2, but headwinds loom ahead
data.description:
Q2 GDP Preview
  • Advance indicators suggest continuation of demand resilience from Q1 to Q2
  • Expect GDP for Q2FY27 at 7.7% with GVA growth at 8.0%
  • See H2FY27 GDP growth weakening to 6.7% Vs H1FY27 GDP growth of 7.8%
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Resilience has been the cornerstone of the Indian economy. There have been many challenges, including the imposition of tariffs by the US, the oil and commodity shock due to the West Asia Crisis, and a sharp currency depreciation in India, associated with AI-led FX outflows on account of FPI selling. However, India’s economy has been solid, averaging a growth of 8 percent over the last four quarters from Q2FY26 to Q1FY27.

Importantly, both industry and services sectors have shown resilience, and it cannot be said that one or the other has been the principal contributor to growth. On the expenditure side, private final consumption expenditure growth averaged 7.3 percent in the same four quarters as mentioned above, higher than the average growth of 6.6 percent in the four quarters before that.

The resilience shown can be ascribed to a) GST rationalization in September 2025, b) the government not allowing full pass-through of the oil shock to end users, even as pump prices of petrol and diesel were increased, and c) fruition of some of the policy initiatives provided by the government – such as the PLI scheme, etc.

On the growth expectations for Q2FY27, we see the resilience continuing. Advance indicators suggest a continuation of the demand resilience from Q1 to Q2. Gross GST revenue growth remains strong in Q2 (this may partially be due to inflation) signaling resilience in demand. GST revenue growth has continued into October, reflecting strong festive demand, along with a pickup in the growth of the e-way Bills. Retail automobile sales in the rural segment remained strong in Q2, with two-wheeler sales (FADA) recording a very healthy growth of 27 percent in Q2 compared to approximately 16 percent in Q1.

Further, a sharp rise in Currency with the Public to 13.8 percent by the end of September, compared to 9.2 percent Y-o-Y in the same period last year, indicates strong consumption demand. The support comes from an increase in personal loan growth at 17 percent Y-o-Y in Q2 compared to an average of 15.7 percent in Q1. Loans for consumer durables, vehicle loans, and credit cards showed higher growth in Q2 than in Q1.

Apart from consumption demand, there are now indications that private capex growth is picking up. A strong pickup in credit flows to industry is visible. While a part of this is due to inventory cost increases, our analysis shows an increase in longer-duration loans, mainly associated with project loans. On the other hand, growth in capital goods and infrastructure goods production within the IIP was at 15.1 percent Y-o-Y and 7.7 percent Y-o-Y in Q2, broadly stable compared to Q1.

Within the Core Index, cement production increased by 11.7 percent Y-o-Y in Q2 compared to 8.9 percent in Q1. On the other hand, steel production was softer at 3.4 percent Y-o-Y in Q2 compared to 5.1 percent in Q1, but improved in both August and September, after a sharp drop in July. Finally, capital goods imports were also strong, suggesting a pickup in private capex.

Based on the above trends, we estimate GDP for Q2FY27 at 7.7 percent with GVA growth at 8.0 percent. This is also higher than RBI’s estimate of 7.2 percent for the quarter. However, looking ahead, we see some likely headwinds to growth. While we do not have any official data on the Kharif output, news reports point to output loss due to weather conditions.

Drought conditions in parts of the country have lowered soil moisture, while winter appears to be setting in late. Consequently, as of 27 November, wheat sowing is down by 11.6 percent and pulses sowing is down by 8.8 percent. Rural wage growth has declined, and along with higher inflation, real wages are low. The above is likely to be a drag on rural growth, while higher inflation along with rate tightening is expected to have a negative impact on urban consumption.

Thus, we anticipate weaker growth in the quarters ahead. Overall, we see H2FY27 GDP growth weakening to 6.7 percent, compared to H1FY27 GDP growth of 7.8 percent. For FY27, GDP is estimated at 7.2 percent but may have an upside bias if some of the above risks do not materialise.

data.title: Daily Voice: Large-cap valuations at historic lows signal further market upside, says Narnolia CIO
data.description:
Shailendra Kumar is the Chief Investment Officer at Narnolia Financial Services
  • Large-cap valuations remain in lowest quartile of their long-term historical range
  • Expect broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps
  • RBI could consider a 25-basis-point rate hike in December meeting
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Large-cap valuations remain in the lowest quartile of their long-term historical range, providing a favourable valuation backdrop for the market rally to sustain and potentially extend further, said Shailendra Kumar, Chief Investment Officer at Narnolia Financial Services, in an interview with Moneycontrol.

He expects the broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps, as mid- and small-cap valuations remain relatively expensive.

Meanwhile, with October CPI inflation rising above 6 percent, the RBI could consider a 25-basis-point rate hike, he said. However, if global commodity and energy inflation moderate, he expects the rate hike to be followed by an extended pause.

Is the frontline index-led market rally sustainable, given the weakness in the broader markets?

Frontline indices have rallied over 15 percent from their early-October lows, supported by a strong Q2FY27 corporate earnings season. More importantly, large-cap valuations remain in the lowest quartile of their long-term historical range, providing a favourable valuation backdrop for the rally to sustain and potentially extend further.

Will corporate earnings and the Union Budget be the key drivers in sustaining the ongoing market rally?

A: Indian corporate earnings have remained strong since early 2026, supported by the consumption recovery following last year’s GST cuts and a renewed momentum in both public and private capex. Nifty 50 earnings growth was limited to mid-single digits during FY25 and FY26, but since Q4FY26, growth has consistently moved closer to 20 percent YoY, signaling a meaningful improvement in the earnings cycle.

Despite this recovery, persistent FII outflows—driven by stronger earnings growth in markets benefiting from the AI investment cycle and concerns over India’s fiscal and macroeconomic position amid the US-Iran conflict—had kept Indian equities subdued. However, India’s resilience in navigating significant geopolitical disruptions is gradually changing investor sentiment.

While the Union Budget may influence near-term market direction, we believe the sustainability of the rally will ultimately be determined by corporate earnings. As long as earnings momentum remains strong, the underlying foundation of the ongoing market rally remains intact.

Do you expect broader markets to take longer to outperform largecaps?

Yes, we expect the broader market to take longer to regain leadership over large caps. The earnings growth differential between small-cap and large-cap companies has narrowed significantly during the Q2FY27 earnings season.

However, mid- and small-cap valuations remain in relatively expensive territory, while large caps continue to trade at attractive, below-average valuations. This valuation gap is likely to favour large caps in the near term.

Which sectors are you structurally bullish on at the moment?

We remain structurally bullish on auto components, precision engineering, healthcare services, insurance, capital markets and banks.

Beyond these sectoral preferences, we maintain strong conviction in leading companies across industries. We believe several of these Indian industry leaders have the potential to evolve into global champions, emerging as dominant players in their respective industries worldwide—what we term “World Toppers.”

Is this the right time to bet on the FMCG sector, given its recent performance and growth prospects?

The Nifty FMCG Index traded at a trailing 12-month P/E of around 30x in October, its lowest valuation level in nearly 15 years. The emergence of D2C brands has intensified competition, challenging the long-established pricing power and distribution-led moat of large listed FMCG companies. However, the funding environment for D2C businesses has moderated in recent times, easing competitive intensity.

Most emerging brands have also struggled to build sizeable franchises, with relatively few scaling to revenues of Rs 1,000 crore or more. Meanwhile, large listed FMCG companies are increasingly willing to acquire emerging brands, strengthening their competitive positioning and widening their portfolio of growth opportunities.

Despite these improving structural dynamics and the sharp around 20 percent rally in FMCG stocks recently, we remain somewhat cautious in the near term, given the uncertain inflation outlook. We believe the sectors bottoming-out process may take longer to play out, although the downside from current levels appears relatively limited.

Do you think AI-led disruption could continue to weigh on valuations in the Indian equity market?

AI-led disruption has been increasingly visible in the IT services sector over the past two years. At a broader level, we believe AI is a positive structural development for businesses, with the potential to enhance productivity and support earnings growth across industries.

However, in the Indian context, the more important question is its eventual impact on white-collar employment and the resulting second-order implications for consumption. While the situation remains encouraging so far, these developments warrant close monitoring as AI adoption accelerates.

Is credit growth nearing its peak for banks? What is your preferred segment within the financial sector?

We believe the banking sector has entered a structural phase of above-trend credit growth, with NIMs also poised to improve from current levels. This strengthens our preference for banks within the financial sector.

We remain equally constructive on select insurance and capital market businesses, which offer attractive long-term structural growth opportunities.

Do you expect the RBI to keep the repo rate unchanged in its December policy meeting, while the US Federal Reserve delivers another rate hike?

With October CPI rising above 6 percent, the RBI could consider a 25 bps rate hike. However, if global commodity and energy inflation moderate, we expect this to be followed by an extended pause.

Meanwhile, the hawkish tone of the US Federal Reserve’s October policy minutes strengthens our expectation of a further 25 bps rate hike by the Fed.

International Gemological Institute, which certifies diamonds, coloured stones and jewellery, achieved the minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirement on November 27 after promoter Blackstone, through its affiliate, offloaded a 1.55 percent stake in the company through open-market transactions.

According to block deal data on Friday, BCP Asia II Topco, an affiliate of Blackstone, sold 67.16 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 280.05 crore. The transaction represented 1.55 percent of the company's paid-up equity capital.

Seven institutional investors, including Stallion Asset and Old Bridge Mutual Fund, acquired the entire stake sold by Blackstone at Rs 417 per share.

Stallion Asset purchased 11.98 lakh equity shares of International Gemological Institute for Rs 49.97 crore, while Old Bridge Mutual Fund acquired 24 lakh shares for Rs 100.08 crore. Citigroup Global Markets Singapore purchased 7.19 lakh shares for Rs 30 crore.

Additionally, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, Susquehanna Pacific, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund each acquired 5.99 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore.

Following the 1.55 percent stake sale, the total shareholding of the promoter and promoter group in International Gemological Institute declined from 76.55 percent to 75 percent of the paid-up equity share capital, while public shareholding increased to 25 percent, the company said in its filing.

Accordingly, the company has achieved the minimum public shareholding requirement.

Shares of International Gemological Institute rose 1.52 percent to close at Rs 429.65 on Friday, after declining 4.8 percent from the day's high.

Aegis Investment Fund buys 0.5% stake in Jagran Prakashan

Meanwhile, Aegis Investment Fund purchased 11 lakh shares of Jagran Prakashan, representing 0.5 percent of its paid-up equity capital, for Rs 7.61 crore.

The shares were purchased at Rs 69.19 apiece.

Jagran Prakashan stock staged a stellar performance on Friday, surging 9.5 percent to Rs 68.26 amid high trading volumes. The stock extended its gains for the third consecutive session.

Tiger Strategies Fund sells shares worth Rs 12 crore in Shalimar Paints

Tiger Strategies Fund-I offloaded 11 lakh shares of Shalimar Paints for Rs 11.88 crore. The shares were sold at Rs 108.01 apiece.

However, Shalimar Paints shares rose 0.43 percent to Rs 108.57, extending their upward trend for the fourth consecutive session. The rally was accompanied by high trading volumes, particularly following a gap-up opening on November 23.

data.description:
-
  • US stocks rallied on Friday, led by tech and chip shares.
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 headed for their best weeks since May.
  • Investors remain cautious amid AI sustainability and rate fears.

US stocks rallied Friday, capping a week of whiplash as dip buyers scooped up some beaten down technology shares despite lingering worries about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence boom.

The S&P 500 Index was up 1.2% as of 10:53 a.m. in New York, while the Nasdaq 100 Index advanced 1.7% after US markets reopened from Thursday’s holiday. Trading will end early at 1 p.m. in New York on Friday.

Stocks have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s chief executive officer and Anthropic PBC’s brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI trade. Anthropic jumped 8.4% Friday. A key gauge of market turbulence — the Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX — was around 26 after briefly spiking to nearly 35 on Wednesday, when markets tumbled early in the session before clawing back the losses.

Nvidia Corp. fell as much as 2.6% and was the biggest point decliner in both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. But a gauge of chip stocks rebounded along with other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm SanDisk Corp., which soared 13%, and Micron Technology Inc., which gained 5.7%. Optical-products maker ​Lumentum Holdings Inc. and server maker Dell Technologies Inc. both gained at least 6%.

The advance left the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 heading for their best weeks since May. The most speculative corners of the market were higher Friday, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s basket of the most-shorted stocks rising 1.5% — with its 7.2% weekly gain on track for its best since August — while a basket of unprofitable tech companies jumping 2.6%.

“Despite any rebounds, this is the most nervous half day of trading for investors that we’ve seen in years, given that there’s not a lot of conviction around Nvidia still,” said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president, head of retail expansion and alternative investment products at Cboe Global Markets.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave Inc. was flat, reversing an earlier sharp rise, while Nebius Group NV rose 2.5% to ease off earlier highs after jumping nearly 6%. AI hyperscalers Meta Platforms Inc. rallied more than 3% while Amazon.com Inc. jumped 2.8%. Apple Inc. rose nearly 1%. Oracle Corp. advanced 1%. A basket of Magnificent Seven stocks rose 1.6%, putting its weekly gain of 7.3% on track for its best since April.

US Chipmakers Rebound

Even with this week’s rebound, the S&P 500 is eyeing its worst November since the height of the 2008 financial crisis as the market is dragged down by concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom, elevated inflation and expectations that the Federal Reserve will resume raising interest rates next month.

Swap traders are almost fully pricing in a quarter-point ​rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in ​the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October.

“There’s still fierce debate over whether the AI trade is over or not,” said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. “Institutions will have to make decisions in the next few weeks over how to move forward and that will set the tone heading into 2027.”

President Donald Trump has also sowed uncertainty with tariff hikes planned on imports from China, Japan, the European Union and other trading partners. Key events to watch next week include Huang’s congressional testimony following his reinstatement at Nvidia and the November US jobs report.

Traders remained optimistic Friday, though, as strong profit outlooks during the crucial holiday season would present a much-needed tailwind. Estimates from the National Retail Federation imply a 4.2% growth in holiday retail sales in 2026 from a year ago, compared with 3.1% in 2025. On Black Friday alone, Americans are expected to spend almost $13 billion in online transactions, data from Adobe Analytics shows.

So far, earnings results from retail companies have been mixed. Earlier this week, Dollar Tree Inc.’s third-quarter adjusted earnings per share and comparable sales topped Wall Street expectations, while Best Buy Co. Inc. raised its guidance for the year on resilient demand for computing. Target Corp.’s sales beat estimates, while TJX Companies Inc. narrowed its earnings outlook.

More retailers will report earnings next week, including Macy’s Inc. and Dollar General Corp.

On Friday, defensive stocks that tend to have comparatively low valuations and offer robust dividends were slipping after outperforming earlier in the week, with Coca-Cola Co., Procter & Gamble Co. and J.M. Smucker Co. all lower.

Investors had flocked to such consumer staples companies in the past few months, putting them on track for the best quarter since 2000. The advance has made valuations look stretched: the S&P 500 Consumer Staples Index is sitting at 24 times projected earnings, the most since the 1990s.

Sectors in Focus

Elsewhere, Altria Group Inc. fell as much as 2.6% after news that the company is considering an offer for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands, potentially in partnership with Japan Tobacco.

Meanwhile, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc. slid 6.9% after the company said the FDA extended the target action date by up to three months for a license application for the use of povetacicept to treat a type of chronic kidney disease.
